questions.q: What did the dashboard/alert audit from Lesson 19 actually find?
options: Nothing — the audit found no other issues
Two real findings: a consumer-lag alert averaged across all pods, and a secondary-cloud health check that aggregated status across node pools
Twenty separate blind spots across the entire platform
That the original incident had actually never happened
questions.explain: An honest audit finds what's actually there — two real, fixable findings, not an exhaustive rewrite and not a clean bill of health.

questions.q: Why does Theo turn the Lesson 22 sale-window ceiling bump into a version-controlled Terraform change instead of a manual kubectl patch?
options: Because manual patches are faster
Because a verbal agreement or manual patch doesn't survive the next person who touches the infrastructure, while a reviewed Terraform change does
Because Terraform doesn't support HPA settings at all
Because Casey specifically forbade using kubectl
questions.explain: Code reviewed in a pull request is durable and auditable; a manual step someone has to remember is not.

questions.q: What does rolling out topologySpreadConstraints as the DEFAULT for every multi-replica deployment accomplish, beyond fixing the one deployment that broke?
options: It closes the same class of risk across the whole cluster at once, rather than waiting for each deployment to have its own incident first
It has no effect beyond the original deployment
It removes the need for a cluster autoscaler
It automatically fixes unrelated cost issues
questions.explain: Making the fix the default for all deployments addresses the risk pattern platform-wide instead of one incident at a time.

questions.q: What does adding a PodDisruptionBudget protect against that topologySpreadConstraints alone does not?
options: Nothing new — they do the exact same thing
A node drain or rolling update voluntarily taking out too many replicas in one zone at once, even if pods were originally spread evenly
Protecting against cost overruns
Protecting against a DNS outage
questions.explain: topologySpreadConstraints controls initial placement; a PodDisruptionBudget limits voluntary disruption afterward, closing a related but different gap.

questions.q: Why is a budget anomaly alert added specifically for the sale-window ceiling bump?
options: So Finance sees the expected spend increase land exactly when and where it's supposed to, instead of discovering it cold in next month's bill
Because the ceiling bump is expected to be a mistake
To automatically cancel the ceiling bump if it triggers
Because Dana no longer trusts Engineering's numbers
questions.explain: The alert gives Finance visibility into an expected, intentional cost event rather than an unexplained one discovered after the fact.
